structured_output.summary: Under 7 CFR 271.2 and 7 U.S.C. 2012(j), a 53-year-old counts as a disabled member only if they receive certain listed benefits: SSI, Social Security Act Title I/II/X/XIV/XVI disability payments, permanent governmental disability retirement, VA total disability, and similar. A general "is disabled" flag plus unnamed "disability benefits" does not meet that test. The prompt also says not to infer unlisted benefit receipt. Head's wages of about $2,139 a month are above the 2026 SSDI earnings limit of $1,690, so Social Security disability is implausible. That leaves Head subject to the gross income test. Gross income of $3,325.75 a month exceeds the FY2026 limit of $1,696 for one person (7 CFR 273.9(a)), so SNAP is $0, which matches the engine. The consensus of $3,576 assumes Head is SNAP-disabled. Even then it needs the $8,389 employer insurance premiums counted as out-of-pocket, or the $2,200 premiums counted twice, to bring net income to zero.
